prompt: How tall was Abraham Lincoln, the tallest US president, in centimetres?
sourceNote: Lincoln was 6 ft 4 in (193 cm).

prompt: The Statue of Liberty was shipped from France in pieces. How many crates?
sourceNote: It crossed the Atlantic in 350 pieces packed into 214 crates.

prompt: Legend says the Dutch bought Manhattan in 1626 for goods worth how many guilders?
sourceNote: The goods were valued at 60 guilders, famously converted to $24.

prompt: How much did the US pay France for the Louisiana Purchase in 1803, in millions of dollars?
sourceNote: The US paid about $15 million for over 2 million km².

prompt: How many yards from the goal line is the penalty spot in football (soccer)?
sourceNote: The penalty mark is 12 yards (11 m) from the goal line.

prompt: How far is the basketball free-throw line from the backboard, in feet?
sourceNote: The free-throw line is 15 ft from the backboard.

prompt: How long is a cricket pitch, in yards?
sourceNote: The pitch is 22 yards (20.12 m) long.

prompt: How many feet apart are the bases on a baseball diamond?
sourceNote: The bases are 90 ft apart.

prompt: How long is a ten-pin bowling lane from the foul line to the head pin, in feet?
sourceNote: The lane is 60 ft from the foul line to the head pin.

prompt: How many Ballon d'Or awards has Lionel Messi won?
sourceNote: Messi has won a record eight Ballon d'Or awards.

prompt: How many Super Bowls did Tom Brady win?
sourceNote: Brady won seven Super Bowls, more than any NFL franchise.

prompt: How many weeks did Roger Federer spend as world No. 1?
sourceNote: Federer was No. 1 for 310 weeks, 237 of them in a row.

prompt: How many weeks did Novak Djokovic spend as world No. 1, the record?
sourceNote: Djokovic holds the record with 428 weeks at No. 1.

prompt: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Serena Williams win?
sourceNote: Serena won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, the Open Era record.

prompt: How many Oscar nominations has Meryl Streep received, the record for an actor?
sourceNote: Streep has 21 Academy Award nominations and three wins.

prompt: In Stanley Kubrick's The Shining, what is the number of the forbidden hotel room?
sourceNote: Kubrick changed it from 217 in the novel to 237.

prompt: In This Is Spinal Tap, Nigel's amplifier goes up to what number?
sourceNote: 'These go to eleven.' The phrase is now an English idiom.

prompt: Han Solo boasts the Millennium Falcon made the Kessel Run in less than how many parsecs?
sourceNote: 'It's the ship that made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs.'

prompt: How many episodes of Star Trek: The Next Generation were made?
sourceNote: TNG ran seven seasons and 178 episodes.

prompt: Tommy Wiseau's cult disaster The Room cost how many million dollars to make?
sourceNote: The Room's budget was about $6 million.

prompt: How many episodes of Bob Ross's The Joy of Painting were made?
sourceNote: The show ran for 31 seasons and 403 episodes.

prompt: How many episodes of Columbo were made?
sourceNote: Columbo ran for 69 episodes from 1968 to 2003.

prompt: How many episodes of the Western series Gunsmoke were made?
sourceNote: Gunsmoke ran 20 seasons and 635 episodes on TV.

prompt: How many consecutive games did Ken Jennings win on Jeopardy! in 2004?
sourceNote: Jennings won 74 games in a row.

prompt: How much money did Ken Jennings win during his 74-game Jeopardy! streak, in dollars?
sourceNote: He won $2,520,700 during the streak.

prompt: How long is Led Zeppelin's 'Stairway to Heaven', in seconds?
sourceNote: The song runs 8 minutes 2 seconds.

prompt: How many acts performed at Woodstock in 1969?
sourceNote: 32 acts played over the weekend.

prompt: How many minutes of audio could the original compact disc hold?
sourceNote: The original CD standard held 74 minutes, long enough for Beethoven's Ninth.

prompt: How many revolutions per minute does a 7-inch vinyl single spin at?
sourceNote: Singles play at 45 rpm. LPs play at 33⅓.

prompt: Apple's original 2001 iPod promised how many songs in your pocket?
sourceNote: The slogan was '1,000 songs in your pocket'.

prompt: What's the most money you can carry in Pokémon Red and Blue?
sourceNote: The money counter maxes out at ₽999,999.

prompt: How many real-time minutes is one full day-night cycle in Minecraft?
sourceNote: A Minecraft day lasts 20 minutes.

prompt: How many obsidian blocks do you need for the smallest complete Nether portal frame in Minecraft (without corners)?
sourceNote: A 4 × 5 frame without its corners uses 10 obsidian.

prompt: How many mines are on the Expert board in classic Windows Minesweeper?
sourceNote: Expert is a 30 × 16 grid with 99 mines.

prompt: How many keys are on a standard full-size US computer keyboard?
sourceNote: A full-size US keyboard has 104 keys.

prompt: What port number does HTTPS use by default?
sourceNote: HTTPS uses port 443 by default.

prompt: What's the maximum possible score in a game of Yahtzee?
sourceNote: A perfect game with every Yahtzee bonus scores 1,575.

prompt: How many squares do all the ships take up in classic Battleship?
sourceNote: Carrier 5, battleship 4, cruiser 3, submarine 3, destroyer 2: 17 squares.

prompt: How many land hexes are on a standard Settlers of Catan board?
sourceNote: The base game board has 19 land hexes.

prompt: How many territories are on the board in the classic game of Risk?
sourceNote: The board has 42 territories on six continents.

prompt: What's the highest level a Pokémon can reach?
sourceNote: Pokémon top out at level 100.

prompt: How many chapters are in the Protestant Bible?
sourceNote: The Protestant Bible has 1,189 chapters.

prompt: How many letters are in the modern Georgian alphabet?
sourceNote: Modern Georgian uses 33 letters.

prompt: How many consonant letters are in the Thai alphabet?
sourceNote: Thai has 44 consonant letters.

prompt: How many grammatical cases do Finnish nouns have?
sourceNote: Finnish nouns have 15 cases.

prompt: How many letters are in the standard Italian alphabet?
sourceNote: Italian uses 21 letters. J, K, W, X and Y appear only in foreign words.

prompt: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of India's constitution?
sourceNote: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages.

prompt: How many official languages does the European Union have?
sourceNote: The EU has 24 official languages.

prompt: How many basic characters are in the modern Japanese hiragana syllabary?
sourceNote: Modern hiragana has 46 basic characters.

prompt: How many litres of water does it take to produce 1 kg of beef?
sourceNote: The average water footprint of beef is about 15,415 litres per kg.

prompt: How many herbs and spices go into Jägermeister?
sourceNote: Jägermeister is made with 56 herbs and spices.

prompt: How many plants, herbs and flowers go into Chartreuse liqueur?
sourceNote: Carthusian monks make it from 130 plants, herbs and flowers.

prompt: Dr Pepper is famously made from how many flavours?
sourceNote: The drink is marketed as a blend of 23 flavours.

prompt: Heinz's famous slogan advertises how many varieties?
sourceNote: The '57 Varieties' slogan dates from 1896.

prompt: How much did a ticket to the first Super Bowl in 1967 cost, in dollars?
sourceNote: The most expensive tickets were $12.

prompt: What was the Mona Lisa insured for in 1962, in millions of dollars?
sourceNote: It was assessed at $100 million for a US tour, the highest insurance valuation ever.

prompt: In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, what's the answer to life, the universe and everything?
sourceNote: Deep Thought computed it over 7.5 million years.

prompt: In George Orwell's 1984, which room number holds your worst fear?
sourceNote: Room 101 contains 'the worst thing in the world'.

prompt: How many Rings of Power were made in Tolkien's legend, counting the One Ring?
sourceNote: Three for the Elves, seven for the Dwarves, nine for Men and the One Ring.

prompt: How many dwarves are in Thorin's company in The Hobbit?
sourceNote: Thorin and his 12 companions make 13 dwarves.

prompt: How old does Bilbo turn at his farewell party at the start of The Lord of the Rings?
sourceNote: Bilbo celebrates his 'eleventy-first' birthday.

prompt: What house number did Sherlock Holmes live at on Baker Street (ignoring the letter)?
sourceNote: Holmes lived at 221B Baker Street.

prompt: About how many oil paintings did Vincent van Gogh make?
sourceNote: He made about 2,100 artworks, including around 860 oil paintings.

prompt: Stubbs the cat served as honorary mayor of Talkeetna, Alaska, for how many years?
sourceNote: Stubbs was 'mayor' from 1997 until his death in 2017.

prompt: Legend says the kingdom will fall if fewer than how many ravens live at the Tower of London?
sourceNote: At least six ravens are kept at the Tower at all times.

prompt: How many drops have fallen in the Pitch Drop Experiment that started in 1927?
sourceNote: Only nine drops have fallen since 1927, and nobody has seen one fall.

prompt: How many Lego bricks stacked on top of each other would reach the top of the Eiffel Tower?
sourceNote: A standard brick is 9.6 mm tall. The Eiffel Tower is 330 m.

prompt: Reading 250 words a minute, how many hours would it take to read War and Peace?
sourceNote: The novel is 587,287 words long.

prompt: How many Statues of Liberty (ground to torch) stacked up would match the Burj Khalifa?
sourceNote: The statue stands 93 m from the ground to the torch. The Burj Khalifa is 828 m.

prompt: How many football pitches (105 m × 68 m) would fit in Monaco?
sourceNote: Monaco covers 2.08 km². A pitch is 7,140 m².

prompt: How many bones are in one adult human hand (including the wrist)?
sourceNote: The hand has 27 bones: 8 carpals in the wrist, 5 metacarpals in the palm and 14 phalanges in the fingers.

prompt: How many bones are in the adult human body?
sourceNote: A typical adult skeleton has 206 bones. Babies are born with around 270, and many fuse together as they grow.

prompt: How many teeth does a full set of adult human teeth have (including wisdom teeth)?
sourceNote: A full adult set is 32 teeth: 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars and 12 molars, including 4 wisdom teeth.

prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
sourceNote: An octopus has three hearts. Two pump blood through the gills and one pumps it around the body.

prompt: How many vertebrae are in a giraffe's neck?
sourceNote: Giraffes have 7 neck vertebrae, the same as humans. Each one can be over 25 cm long.

prompt: How many chemical elements are on the periodic table?
sourceNote: 118 elements have been discovered and named. The last four (113, 115, 117 and 118) were named in 2016.

prompt: The speed of light in a vacuum, in kilometres per second (rounded down to a whole number)?
sourceNote: The speed of light is defined as exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, about 299,792 km per second.

prompt: The average distance from Earth to the Moon, in kilometres?
sourceNote: The average Earth to Moon distance is about 384,400 km. It varies between roughly 363,000 and 405,000 km over each orbit.

prompt: The height of Mount Everest in metres (2020 survey)?
sourceNote: A joint China and Nepal survey in 2020 measured Everest at 8,848.86 m above sea level.

prompt: The height of Mount Logan, Canada's tallest mountain, in metres?
sourceNote: Mount Logan in Yukon is 5,959 m tall, the highest peak in Canada and the second highest in North America.

prompt: The height of Toronto's CN Tower, in metres?
sourceNote: The CN Tower is 553.3 m tall. It was the world's tallest free-standing structure from 1975 until 2007.

prompt: How many steps are in the CN Tower's stairwell (the one used for charity climbs)?
sourceNote: The CN Tower's stairwell has 1,776 steps, climbed every year in charity stair-climb events.

prompt: The architectural height of Dubai's Burj Khalifa, in metres?
sourceNote: The Burj Khalifa's architectural height is 828 m, the tallest building in the world since 2010.

prompt: The total length of all sections of the Great Wall of China, in kilometres (2012 Chinese government survey)?
sourceNote: A 2012 survey by China's State Administration of Cultural Heritage measured all sections of the wall at 21,196 km.

prompt: The official length of a marathon, in metres?
sourceNote: The marathon was fixed at 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards) in 1921, based on the 1908 London Olympics course.

prompt: How many keys are on a standard modern piano?
sourceNote: Modern pianos have 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black, covering just over seven octaves.

prompt: How many spaces are around the edge of a standard Monopoly board?
sourceNote: A Monopoly board has 40 spaces: 28 properties, 3 Chance, 3 Community Chest, 2 taxes and 4 corners.

prompt: How many tiles come in a standard English-language Scrabble set?
sourceNote: The standard English Scrabble set has 100 tiles, including 2 blanks.

prompt: Add up every number on a European roulette wheel (0 to 36). What's the total?
sourceNote: A European wheel has the numbers 0 to 36. Added together they total 666, which is why roulette is nicknamed 'the devil's game'.

prompt: How many pips (dots) are there in total across a standard double-six domino set?
sourceNote: A double-six set has 28 tiles. Each number from 0 to 6 appears 8 times, so the pips total 8 × 21 = 168.

prompt: How many member states does the United Nations have?
sourceNote: The UN has 193 member states. The most recent to join was South Sudan in 2011.

prompt: How many UN member states are in Africa?
sourceNote: Africa has 54 UN member states, more than any other continent.

prompt: How many time zones does Russia use?
sourceNote: Russia uses 11 time zones, from UTC+2 in Kaliningrad to UTC+12 in Kamchatka.

prompt: How many provinces and territories does Canada have, combined?
sourceNote: Canada has 10 provinces and 3 territories. Nunavut, the newest, was created in 1999.

prompt: How many regular-season NHL goals did Wayne Gretzky score in his career?
sourceNote: Wayne Gretzky scored 894 regular-season NHL goals, a record that stood until Alex Ovechkin passed it in 2025.

prompt: How many regular-season NHL points (goals + assists) did Wayne Gretzky record in his career?
sourceNote: Gretzky finished with 2,857 regular-season points (894 goals and 1,963 assists), still the NHL record.

prompt: How many Pokémon are in the original Pokédex of Pokémon Red and Blue?
sourceNote: Pokémon Red and Blue (1996 in Japan) have 151 Pokémon, from Bulbasaur to Mew.

prompt: How many episodes of Breaking Bad were made?
sourceNote: Breaking Bad ran for 62 episodes over 5 seasons, from 2008 to 2013.

prompt: How many episodes of Friends were made, across all 10 seasons?
sourceNote: Friends ran for 236 episodes over 10 seasons, from 1994 to 2004.

prompt: How many official Eon Productions James Bond films have been released (up to No Time to Die)?
sourceNote: Eon Productions released 25 Bond films from Dr. No (1962) to No Time to Die (2021).

prompt: How many minutes are in a 365-day year?
sourceNote: 365 days × 24 hours × 60 minutes = 525,600 minutes, the number in the song from Rent.

prompt: Roughly how many times does a heart beating at 70 beats per minute beat in one day?
sourceNote: A resting adult heart usually beats 60 to 100 times a minute. At 70 bpm that's 100,800 beats a day.

prompt: How many double stitches are on an official MLB baseball?
sourceNote: A Major League baseball has 108 double stitches.

prompt: How many letters are in the alphabet of Rotokas, a language of Papua New Guinea with one of the smallest alphabets?
sourceNote: The Rotokas alphabet has just 12 letters.

prompt: How many seconds long is 'Me at the zoo', the first video uploaded to YouTube?
sourceNote: The 2005 clip of co-founder Jawed Karim at San Diego Zoo is 19 seconds long.

prompt: How many dots (not counting the 4 power pellets) are in the Pac-Man maze?
sourceNote: Each maze has 240 dots and 4 power pellets.

prompt: How many men were on Shackleton's Endurance expedition ship, all of whom survived?
sourceNote: All 28 men of the Endurance crew survived after the ship was crushed by ice.
